gaps.sentence: Her kindness and ___ (GENEROUS) made her very popular.
gaps.explanation: Parallel to 'kindness', a noun is needed: generosity (note the irregular -osity spelling).

gaps.sentence: I'm afraid your passport is ___ — it expired last month (VALID).
gaps.hint: negative adjective needed: it has expired
gaps.explanation: An expired document is invalid (in- + valid); an adjective is needed after 'is'.

gaps.hint: person needed (-ist for fields of study)
gaps.explanation: The suffix -ist forms the person who studies a subject: biology becomes biologist.

gaps.sentence: We must take ___ for our own health (RESPONSIBLE).
gaps.explanation: 'Take responsibility for something' is the fixed phrase; the -ity noun is needed.

gaps.sentence: Her answer was ___ , so we had to ask again (RELEVANT).
gaps.hint: negative adjective needed — it did not relate to the question
gaps.explanation: The negative of 'relevant' is 'irrelevant' (ir- before r). An adjective is needed after 'was'.

gaps.sentence: It is ___ to book tickets in advance during the festival (ADVICE).
gaps.explanation: The suffix -able forms the adjective: advisable means worth recommending. 'It is + adjective + to-infinitive'.

gaps.sentence: He had a happy ___ in the countryside (CHILD).
gaps.hint: noun needed: the period of being a child (-hood)
gaps.explanation: The suffix -hood forms period-of-life nouns: childhood.

gaps.sentence: It is ___ to smoke inside public buildings (LEGAL).
gaps.hint: negative adjective needed: against the law (il-)
gaps.explanation: The negative of 'legal' is 'illegal' (il- before l). An adjective is needed after 'is'.
